transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’ve been kind of arranging my days so I don’t have to use elevators. Like taking the stairs at home, even if it’s five flights. I turned down a workshop because it was in a high-rise, and I stopped visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn’t really have another option.
When you avoid elevators, is it because you're worried something might happen to you in there, like feeling trapped or having a panic attack?

Yeah… sort of. I know, logically, elevators in office buildings are probably safe. But when I see the older doors in my apartment building or at work, I just… my brain goes straight to getting stuck, or it dropping. I know that sounds excessive.
Do you find yourself avoiding other situations or places where you might feel trapped or anxious, like crowded spaces or public transportation?
Not really… I don’t think so. I mean, I use buses and crowded places okay enough. It’s mostly the elevator thing that gets to me.
Have you ever felt the same kind of anxiety or avoidance about any other situations or places outside of elevators?
Not that I’ve really noticed. I mean… nothing that makes me go out of my way like elevators do.
Do you ever feel anxious or avoid places that are very open, like parking lots, bridges, or large fields?
No… I don’t think so. Parking lots or open places don’t really bother me like that.
Do you ever feel anxious or avoid situations where you might be at a height, such as standing near the edge of a balcony or climbing a ladder?
Not really. Heights don’t stand out to me like that… I mean, I might be careful on a ladder, but I don’t avoid it or anything.
